title: November Twenty-Six (Pete McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit storytelling 104bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal warm celebration
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
November twenty-six, the year was good
A baby came into the neighbourhood
Biggest one we'd seen in quite some time
Wilma said — this boy is going to be fine

[Verse 2]
Years went by, he grew into his boots
Oldest son don't need to prove his roots
Rugby in the winter, sun out on the bay
Fifty-something now but still that same old way

[Chorus]
November twenty-six, raise a glass
To the one who always showed the rest what class
Pete Capitán, the first one through the door
Happy birthday to the one who set the floor

[Bridge]
Chas is watching from the stands
Couldn't be more proud of these two hands
Oldest first and that's the way it goes
November twenty-six — that's how the story goes

[Verse 3]
Pelican out on the water calm and sure
Same man every morning, nothing to prove more
Charter boat and sunrise, salt air in his hair
November twenty-six — he's always been right there

[Outro]
Happy birthday Pete
Happy birthday mate
That's my boy
That's my boy
